correctness.rationale: For every even length k=2m, the elementary even-period identity gives G=F_m (m even) or L_m (m odd). An independently proved cubic Cassini lemma computes the exact gcd D of the two successive cube differences, including every prime and its valuation. D divides all shifted cube differences. The telescoping initial-sum identity proves D divides 2S_0 and precisely determines its parity quotient: odd if and only if 3 divides m, yielding gcd(D,S_0)=D or D/2. Finite exact recurrence tests for 120 even lengths and 2400 windows agree; they are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A 2022 published study explicitly poses the even-length cubic Fibonacci-gcd problem and proposes a case split. This theorem resolves the complete infinite family with a proved, nontrivial correction to that split. The structural Cassini-root and 2-adic analysis explain extra factors 3 and 1/2 and provide a reusable arithmetic approach to higher powers and other recurrence families. This is a natural infinite classification, not an arbitrary finite special case or isolated counterexample.
